title: Cut elimination for intuitionistic propositional sequents

based_on.title: Constructive Logic: Cut Elimination (Lecture 10, October 5, 2017; edits by Andre Platzer)

summary: Remove cuts from native intuitionistic sequent proofs by syntactic replacement, retaining one conclusion and explicit constructive negation.
abstract: An intermediate lemma can make a proof easier to find, but it can also hide why its conclusion follows from its assumptions. We show that every finite intuitionistic propositional proof can be rebuilt without such intermediate cuts. The construction keeps exactly one conclusion, handles implication by supplying its input before using its output, and follows both possible branches of a disjunction. Its resulting proof contains only components of the end formulas, apart from the explicitly tracked falsum used by negation. This gives a syntactic proof of consistency and a foundation for reading constructive witnesses from proofs.
